transcript:
Meeting header: 2026-03-25 15:00 UTC | Duration: 48 mins | Attendees: Priya Shah (Redwood AE), Miguel Torres (Redwood SE), Laura Chen (CTO, Omnix), Raj Patel (Platform), Marta Oliveira (Data Scientist)

[00:00] Priya Shah: Hey everyone, thanks for making time. Quick intro, I'm Priya, AE at Redwood, and with me is Miguel from our SE team. How's everyone doing?
[00:12] Laura Chen: Good, thanks. Busy week but excited to dig in.
[00:18] Miguel Torres: Hi all, quick overview goal for today is to understand your integration needs — SDKs, orchestration patterns, LangChain/LlamaIndex usage, and any observability or security constraints.
[00:30] Raj Patel: Perfect. At Omnix we run clinical document processing that touches PHI-adjacent data. We're evaluating whether to use Redwood Hosted for quick spin-up, Dedicated for predictable throughput, or Private for strict network isolation. Primary concerns: latency for real-time triage (~200ms p50 target for short prompts), rate limiting, and auditability.
[01:05] Priya Shah: Understood. Can you tell us about your current stack and where you'd like Redwood to sit? Are you thinking direct SDK calls from app servers, a central gateway, or sidecar pattern?
[01:20] Laura Chen: Our APIs are in Go and Node, running in Kubernetes. We currently route external ML calls through an internal API gateway; we prefer not to have each service hold credentials. So a gateway/proxy pattern is what we're leaning toward, but we want to understand any latency tradeoffs.
[01:40] Miguel Torres: Gateway is common. From an observability angle, we recommend adding request IDs and passing tracing headers through. On Hosted, you can use short-lived API keys, but Dedicated or Private lets you keep KMS inside your VPC. Gateway adds one hop — usually 20-50ms depending on your infra — but you gain centralized auth, quota enforcement, and caching.
[02:10] Marta Oliveira: About SDKs — do you have official Go and Node SDKs, and what about Python for LangChain and LlamaIndex integrations?
[02:24] Priya Shah: Yes — official SDKs in Node, Python, and Go. For LangChain and LlamaIndex there's community adapters plus our maintained examples. Miguel, can you walk through the LangChain integration patterns?
[02:36] Miguel Torres: Sure. Two common patterns: 1) Use Redwood's Python SDK directly in the LangChain LLM wrapper — standard and easiest for experiments. 2) For production, wrap calls behind your gateway and implement a slim LangChain connector that hits your internal endpoint. For LlamaIndex, we provide example prompt helpers and index sharding notes. Note sometimes our examples reference older product names or minor typos in docs — we'll send cleaned examples.
[03:10] Raj Patel: If we go through gateway, how do you handle rate limits and quotas? We need per-tenant quotas and burst protection.
[03:22] Miguel Torres: On Hosted we offer configurable rate limits at the API key level and per-route. For Dedicated, you can set quota policies in the console and enforce per-tenant via API keys or JWT claims. For Private, you manage rate limiting in your proxy but Redwood supports headers for quota reporting and can accept x-client-id headers to attribute usage. We also expose a token-level cost breakdown in the console for billing.
[04:00] Laura Chen: For observability, we need request-level tracing tied to our tracing system (we use Jaeger/OpenTelemetry). Does Redwood emit spans or integrate with OTEL?
[04:15] Miguel Torres: We emit request logs and provide tracing hooks. For Dedicated and Private, you can forward structured logs to your collectors and pass through tracing headers. Hosted provides webhook hooks and S3 log exports. We'll share our observability integration guide.
[04:40] Marta Oliveira: Do you support streaming responses for partial tokens? Our triage UI streams short completions.
[04:48] Priya Shah: Yes, streaming is supported on Hosted and Dedicated, and on Private if you enable the streaming endpoint. Keep in mind that streaming may affect latency SLOs depending on your gateway buffering.
[05:05] Raj Patel: Security — SOC2, encryption, KMS, and audit logs are mandatory for us. Also need to know about data retention and deletion paths.
[05:18] Miguel Torres: We're SOC 2 Type II. Hosted encrypts data at rest and in transit; we provide KMS integrations for Dedicated and Private. Audit logs are available in the console and via API. For data residency, Dedicated and Private allow you to choose regions; Private is the option for strict on-prem or air-gapped needs. We'll attach the security matrix and SOC2 report.
[05:45] Laura Chen: If we move forward with Dedicated, what does capacity look like, and how do you handle burst patterns? Our workload has diurnal spikes and occasional overnight batch jobs.
[05:58] Priya Shah: Dedicated gives you reserved GPU pools with autoscaling and burst options. You can configure autoscale policies by route and set a guaranteed baseline. For bursty batch we recommend a separate pool or scheduled capacity. We can propose pricing tiers based on your QPS and token volumes once you share sample payloads.
[06:20] Raj Patel: About model variants and quantization — can we pin older versions or use quantized variants for cost savings?
[06:30] Miguel Torres: Yes. The platform supports model version pinning and quantized variants. For certain models we run optimized kernels and suggest quantization profiles depending on your latency and quality tradeoffs. Redwood Optimize can recommend profiles by workload.
[06:50] Marta Oliveira: We use LangChain agents and often need function/tool calling with structured outputs. Any caveats?
[06:58] Miguel Torres: Function calling is supported. For structured output, we suggest schema enforcement on the client and post-parse checks. If using gateway, ensure you forward content-type and any schema headers so we can maintain tracing.
[07:20] Priya Shah: Can you walk us through a sample flow for a short prompt: app -> gateway -> Redwood -> back, including headers you'd want?
[07:30] Raj Patel: Sure. App sends request to internal gateway with x-request-id, x-tenant-id, and tracing headers. Gateway authenticates and routes to Redwood endpoint, injecting x-client-id. We'd expect Redwood to return request_id and token usage in response headers for correlation.
[07:50] Miguel Torres: Exactly. We recommend returning x-rr-request-id and x-usage-tokens headers. Our SDKs automatically attach and parse these, but if you go through a proxy we provide middleware snippets for common gateways like Envoy and Kong.
[08:10] Laura Chen: About SDK placement — is it safe to call directly from our backend services, or should we always route via a proxy?
[08:20] Miguel Torres: For smaller teams or experiments, direct SDK calls are fine. For production multi-tenant systems, proxy/gateway gives centralized auth, per-tenant quotas, and easier rotation of keys. It also simplifies caching and prefix dedupe.
[08:40] Raj Patel: How does prefix/KV caching work if multiple services use the same model? Can caching be shared?
[08:52] Miguel Torres: On Dedicated and Private, you can configure shared KV caches to reuse prefixes across requests. Hosted also supports caching but with tenant isolation. Shared caches improve downstream latency if you have repeated prompts. We'll include caching patterns in the guide.
[09:10] Marta Oliveira: Any gotchas with LlamaIndex connectors and retrieval augmented generation (RAG)?
[09:18] Miguel Torres: Mostly around embedding dimension compatibility and batch sizes. For embeddings we suggest separate routes with different quotas and batching configs. Also, if you plan to shard indexes across nodes, watch out for sequence length limits and tokenization differences. Our embeddings API includes versioning to avoid silent mismatches.
[09:48] Priya Shah: Timeline — what's your ideal timeline for a pilot?
[09:55] Laura Chen: We'd like a two-week pilot to validate latency and cost, and a broader pilot across three teams over 6-8 weeks. Budget cycle aligns with early May procurement.
[10:10] Priya Shah: OK, so we can aim for pilot kickoff first week of April. For the pilot we'll need sample payloads, target SLOs, and success criteria.
[10:20] Raj Patel: Success criteria: p50 < 250ms for short prompts, p95 < 600ms; token cost under X (we'll provide target), and full audit logs available per request.
[10:35] Miguel Torres: Noted. For baseline testing we can run a 48-hour benchmark to establish p50/p95 against Hosted and Dedicated variants. We'll provide scripts you can run from your environment.
[10:55] Laura Chen: Can you share SDK examples for us to prototype LangChain usage quickly?
[11:02] Miguel Torres: Yes, I'll send a LangChain adapter and a small example notebook. Also include a Docker example for running the SDK behind an Envoy sidecar.
[11:18] Priya Shah: Pricing questions — are you able to share a hosted per-token price and Dedicated baseline?
[11:25] Priya Shah: For Hosted we have per-token tiers with volume discounts. Dedicated is a reserved commit model; pricing depends on GPU types and committed throughput. I'll share a preliminary price sheet in the follow-up.
[11:40] Raj Patel: One more — network egress and data residency, for Hosted can you guarantee logs stay in region?
[11:48] Miguel Torres: Hosted stores data in the region selected at project creation. For strict residency and on-prem storage, Private is the path. We'll include region details in the security doc.
[12:10] Marta Oliveira: Any limits on model parallelism or sequence length we need to plan for in the pilot?
[12:18] Miguel Torres: Sequence length limits depend on the model. We'll provide the performance profiles per model and recommended batching configs. For parallelism, Dedicated gives deterministic throughput per pool; we'll recommend pool sizes.
[12:40] Laura Chen: Are there any open-source SDKs or Terraform modules for infra as code?
[12:47] Priya Shah: Yes — we have Terraform modules for Dedicated provisioning and example k8s manifests for Private. We'll share links.
[13:05] Raj Patel: Integration testing — does Redwood have test harnesses to run against staging endpoints?
[13:12] Miguel Torres: We can provide a sandbox project and ephemeral keys for your staging, plus a test harness for load and correctness tests.
[13:30] Laura Chen: Great. On governance, we use SAML/SSO and SCIM for user provisioning. Can Redwood integrate with SSO for console access?
[13:38] Priya Shah: Yes — SAML SSO and SCIM are supported on enterprise plans. We'll include steps for setting up SSO in Dedicated/Private.
[13:55] Marta Oliveira: Any notes on data deletion APIs? We need programmatic deletion of inputs for audits.
[14:03] Miguel Torres: We provide delete-by-request-id endpoints and retention policies configurable per project. For Hosted, deletions are logged; for Private you control retention.
[14:25] Priya Shah: Ok wrapping up, to confirm next steps: we'll send integration guide, security matrix, LangChain adapter repo, pricing sheet, and scheduling the SE deep-dive. Customer to send sample payloads and QPS numbers.
[14:40] Laura Chen: Sounds good. Thanks everyone.
[14:44] Raj Patel: Thanks — we'll aim to have the sample data by end of week.
[14:48] Miguel Torres: I'll follow up with the adapter and a short benchmark script.
[14:52] Priya Shah: Great. We'll set up the deep-dive for the week of April 6th and include an initial pilot plan.
[14:58] Laura Chen: Thanks, bye.

Notes: transcript contains minor transcription artifacts and occasional name spelling variance. Shared links referenced during call: integration-guide.pdf (link to be sent), security-matrix.pdf, langchain-adapter repo (link to be shared).
